headline: Approved steps toward a flow control ordinance for residential recycling, including a City Attorney opinion on solid waste tax collection.
summary: DPW presented a strategy to address a $165,000 budget shortfall in the recycling and solid waste budget. The short-term plan would require residential properties to pay the solid waste generation tax through an ordinance change, which is estimated to capture around 900 additional residential units and increase receipts by $130,000. The committee unanimously approved a motion directing DPW staff to draft ordinance language and obtain a City Attorney opinion.
decisions: Approved, by unanimous vote, a motion directing DPW staff to work with the City Attorney's office to draft ordinance language allowing flow control for residential recycling collection and to obtain an opinion on the existing ordinance.

4. Deliberative Agenda 
 4.1 Solid Waste Generation Tax 
Lee Perry, Division Director Right of Way presented information. 
 
Councilor Bergman is in favor of moving with short term flow control.  Would like a memo 
dedicated to flow control.   Self-haulers – need to justify lower rates. Councilor Broderick is in 
favor of ordinance change and would like to see the memo on flow control.  Believes all RDU’s 
should be charge the solid waste tax.  Chair Barlow supportive of trying to close the gap in the 
short term.  Still missing data. 
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions: DPW presented a proposed strategy to 
address a $165,000 budget shortfall in the recycling and solid waste budget, primarily driven
by declining residential units and increasing diesel fuel prices. The short-term strategy includes 
implementing flow control through an ordinance change to require residential properties to pay 
the solid waste generation tax and transition to municipal collection, which is estimated to 
capture around 900 additional residential units and increase receipts by $130,000. The 
committee was asked for feedback on supporting the ordinance change and moving forward 
with the flow control implementation.  The discussion also covered the potential expansion of 
the solid waste tax to include self-haulers and the possibility of tiered pricing, though more data 
is needed to understand the impact on large apartment buildings and haulers.  DPW proposed 
delaying a broader conversation about applying taxes to all residential dwelling units while 
managing flow control, suggesting implementation by January 1st to provide fiscal relief for 
FY27. 
Councilor Bergman moves to have DPW staff 1) work with the City Attorney’s office to draft 
ordinance language that would allow for flow control for residential recycling collection and any 
ancillary changes that would be necessary to support this updated ordinance, and 2) obtain an 
opinion from the City Attorney’s office on existing ordinance and its applicability to flow control 
authority and Solid Waste Generation Tax collection practices. These two items should be 
circulated to TEUC members in advance of, and preparation for, the City Council meeting on 
October 26th. 
Councilor Broderick seconds.  
All in favor, Unanimous approval
